title: Softmax with Temperature: Distilling Knowledge

paper.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network

hook: How can a neural network teach another network? The secret is in the softmax temperature. Adjust the logits and temperature to see how the probability distribution changes.

equation.caption: Softmax with temperature T. When T=1, it's the standard softmax.

steps: Divide each exponential by the sum to get \(q_i\).

explorations.title: Effect of high temperature
explorations.predict: What happens to the probabilities when T is very large?
explorations.observe: The probabilities become nearly uniform, each close to 0.25.
explorations.why: As T increases, the exponent z_i/T becomes small, so exp(z_i/T) ≈ 1 + z_i/T. The differences between classes shrink, making the distribution approach uniform.

explorations.title: Effect of low temperature
explorations.predict: What happens to the probabilities when T is very small?
explorations.observe: The largest logit dominates: its probability is close to 1, others close to 0.
explorations.why: As T decreases, z_i/T becomes large in magnitude. The exponential of the largest z_i/T dominates the sum, so its probability approaches 1.

limitation: This demonstration uses only 4 logits and a single temperature parameter. In real knowledge distillation, the teacher and student networks have many more classes, and the temperature is tuned along with other hyperparameters. Also, the softmax with temperature is applied to the teacher's logits to produce soft targets, but the student is trained on both soft targets and true labels.
misconception: Temperature does not change the ranking of the logits; it only changes the confidence of the predicted probabilities. The most likely class remains the same for any T > 0.

claims.text: Softmax with temperature T is defined as q_i = exp(z_i/T) / sum_j exp(z_j/T).
High temperature produces a softer probability distribution over classes.
In our toy setup, we use 4 logits and allow the user to adjust them and T to see the effect on the probabilities.

outcomes.outcome: Explain how temperature affects the softmax distribution.
Recognize that high T approaches uniform distribution.
